title: Applied ML Evals: Integration Playbook - Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Model Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization, Regression Triage
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's applied-ML evaluation practices into a single, actionable reference. It defines the end-to-end flow for: eval-harness usage, constructing and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profiling, and regression triage. The goal is to ensure model changes are measured, auditable, and safe for production rollouts while minimizing cost and latency regressions.

Scope
-----
Applies to: model onboarding and updates for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; cross-functional teams including Applied ML, Serving Runtime, Product, and SRE.

Key outcomes
- Reproducible evals for release decisions
- Standardized prompt sets and benchmark cadence
- Clear quantization guidance to balance cost vs. quality
- Fast, prioritized regression triage and rollback criteria

Roles & ownership
-----------------
- Model Owner (applied-ml): coordinates onboarding, provides training data and baseline metrics.
- Eval Lead (applied-ml): maintains eval-harness configurations, test suites, and prompt sets.
- Runtime Owner (eng-serving-runtime): provides perf profiles and quantization support.
- SRE / Oncall: validates SLO impact and executes rollback or routing policies.
- Product PM: approves quality guardrail thresholds for customer-facing features.

Definitions & SLOs
------------------
- Evaluation run: deterministic job in the eval-harness that produces quality and perf metrics.
- Regression: any statistically significant drop in a prioritized metric (precision, BLEU, ROUGE, instruction-following score) or >5% increase in median latency for critical routes.
- Quality SLOs (example):
  - Instruction accuracy (task-specific): >= 90% for core intents
  - Hallucination rate (measured via human-labeled set): <= 3%
  - Median token latency (hosted): <= 75 ms for p50 on targeted generation routes

Onboarding checklist (model->production)
----------------------------------------
1. Pre-onboarding (applied-ml):
   - Provide model artifact (format, weights, tokenizer) and model card.
   - Submit baseline eval report (local dev results) and target use cases.
2. Eval-harness setup (Eval Lead):
   - Add model to eval-harness config (pipeline id, tokenizer mapping, decode params).
   - Configure benchmark suites: smoke, functional, adversarial, and cost/perf.
3. Prompt sets (see Prompt Sets section)
4. Quantization profile (see Quantization Profiles)
5. Performance benchmarking (Runtime Owner):
   - Run perf-suite at relevant sequence lengths and batch sizes.
   - Produce kernels/compilation suggestions and expected p50/p95 numbers.
6. Safety & guardrails (Product/Security):
   - Run guardrail tests (toxicity, PII leakage, privacy checks).
7. Canary rollout plan (SRE/Product):
   - Canary at 1% traffic for 24h, expand to 10% for 48h if no regressions.
8. Production launch and monitoring hooks (Eng-Platform):
   - Add dashboards, alerts, and cost-tracking per route/model/version.

Prompt sets and benchmarks
--------------------------
Guidelines for constructing prompt sets:
- Representative coverage: include common user intents (70%), edge cases (20%), and adversarial inputs (10%).
- Labeling: every input must have a ground-truth or human-evaluated reference score when applicable.
- Versioning: store prompt set metadata: name, owner, creation_date, intended-use, labels.
- Size guidance: smoke (50-200 samples), functional (1k-5k), benchmark (5k-50k) depending on the task.

Benchmark cadence:
- Pre-release: run full benchmark suite (functional + adversarial + perf) on every model candidate.
- Nightly: reduced suite for active release branches (smoke + top-10 intents).
- Weekly: regressions sweep across all shipped models.

Example prompt-set metadata (YAML snippet):
```yaml
name: conversational-helpdesk-v1
owner: applied-ml-team
created_at: 2026-06-01
intended_use: helpdesk summarization and response generation
size: 12000
labels: [conversation, english, helpdesk, regression-critical]
```

Eval harness usage (practical)
------------------------------
- Command-line example (run a named suite):
```bash
# Run functional suite for model v2 on GPU pool 'dev-eval'
eval-harness run --suite functional --model-id model-v2 --pool dev-eval --out results/model-v2-functional-2026-07-01.json
```
- Required outputs: per-sample scores, aggregated metrics, confidence intervals, and artifacts (predictions, logs).
- Storage: attach results to the model's evaluation artifacts bucket and link in the model card.

Quality guardrails
------------------
Guardrails are the automated and manual checks that gate model promotion.
Primary guardrail categories:
- Functional correctness (task metrics)
- Safety (toxicity, PII, malware prompts)
- Stability (variance across prompt paraphrases)
- Latency/cost (should not exceed 5% unit-cost increase without approval)

Promotion policy (example):
- PASS: All critical guardrails within thresholds. Auto-approve to canary.
- REVIEW_REQUIRED: Non-critical regressions or borderline metrics. Requires eval lead + product sign-off.
- FAIL: Critical regressions (e.g., >5% absolute drop in instruction accuracy, safety failure). Block rollout and open regression ticket.

Quantization profiles
---------------------
Goals: reduce memory and cost while keeping quality within acceptable bounds.
Profile creation steps:
1. Baseline (fp16/bf16) evaluation for quality and perf.
2. Candidate quantizations: 8-bit, 4-bit, mixed precision.
3. Per-profile eval: run benchmark suite focusing on instruction-following and safety tests.
4. Accept/reject criteria: quality delta <= 1.5% absolute on prioritized metrics AND no safety failures.

Example quantization test matrix (table):
| profile_name | backend | precision | expected_mem_reduction | q_quality_delta_threshold | owner |
| conversational-8bit | triton-v5 | int8 | ~40% | <= 1.5% | eng-serving-runtime |
| conversational-4bit | custom-kernel | int4 | ~65% | <= 3.0% | eng-serving-runtime |

Notes: Always include calibration runs for int8/4-bit and capture per-layer sensitivity. For customer-sensitive models, run quantization in private deployment mirrors.

Regression triage playbook
--------------------------
When an automated regression is detected (nightly sweep or canary):
1. Triage owner: Eval Lead picks up the alert within 2 hours.
2. Reproduce: re-run the failing suite with the exact model artifact and seed.
3. Classify impact:
   - Severity P0: safety regression or critical functionality drop (>5% absolute) -> Pager and block rollout.
   - Severity P1: significant perf regression (>10% increase in p95 latency) -> Notify runtime + SRE, consider fallback to prior model version.
   - Severity P2: small quality drift or minor perf change -> Create regression ticket and assign to model owner.
4. Root cause checklist:
   - Is this due to model weights or tokenization changes?
   - Is quantization or kernel change implicated? (check perf logs and compile diffs)
   - Are prompt set changes or evaluation config differences causing false positives?
5. Mitigation options (ordered):
   - Roll back model routing to previous stable version.
   - Route affected traffic to a lower-latency region or Dedicated pool.
   - Apply hotfix: tweak decode params or prompt templates.
6. Postmortem: Every P0/P1 must have a postmortem with timeline, RCA, and action items within 7 days.

Monitoring & dashboards
-----------------------
Minimum dashboards to add for each model version:
- Quality dashboard: top-level metrics (accuracy, F1, hallucination rate) with change-over-time and per-prompt-set breakdown.
- Perf dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency by route and sequence length histogram.
- Cost dashboard: tokens per request, throughput, and estimated $/10k tokens.
- Safety dashboard: toxicity scores and PII detection rate.

Templates & examples
--------------------
- Model card template: include model metadata, eval summary, known weaknesses, and recommended default decode params.
- Canary plan template: cadence, traffic ramp, monitoring checklist, rollback criteria.

Appendix: quick checklists
-------------------------
Small checklist for a canary release:
- [ ] Eval-harness: full functional + safety suite PASS
- [ ] Perf: p95 within expected budget for primary routes
- [ ] Quantization: selected profile validated (if used)
- [ ] Dashboards configured and alerts enabled
- [ ] Oncall and model owner contacts listed in release notes
